A brick dog streaks flat out along the grass, all four legs a blur, jaws clamped on a trailing rope that bows behind it in a long low arc.
A stack of round-brick gas cylinders goes over one after another across the grass, each one nudging the next in a slow toppling chain toward the hedgerow.
A trans-orange spark spits from a burner as it catches, the glow spreading outward across the smooth unmarked chrome cylinder surface in a sudden bright wash.
A tarpaulin fabric element snatched off a trailer snaps flat against the hedgerow, pinned there by the gust, its corners quivering against the moulded foliage bricks.
A shower of trans-pink blossom plates drifts across the whole field from the orchard row, spinning slowly as they settle across green plate mosaic and basket rims alike.
A flock of brick swifts scatters upward through the gap between two balloons, wing plates tilted at every angle, the outermost birds banking hard away into open sky.
A brick beehive knocked from its post spills a scatter of yellow studs across the plate mosaic in a wide fan, the round-brick hive body rolling to rest in the tuft elements.
A herd of brick cows breaks across the far grass in a ragged spread, hooves clicking plate seams, the rearmost one still mid-turn with its head low and tail up.
A kite on a long bar-and-clip line tangles itself into a set of load tapes, pulling the taut runs sideways and setting the whole basket rim swaying on its corner uprights.
A swarm of loose trans-clear soap-bubble elements drifts up through the gaps between the balloons, each one catching the light differently as it rises and slowly spins.
A flock of trans-pink brick flamingos lifts off a trans-blue plate lagoon at the field edge, legs still trailing behind, wing plates flared wide in a ragged pink arc.
Trans-clear rain rods slant across the field at a sharp angle, beading in a row of tiny drops along the smooth unmarked wicker-pattern basket rim and pooling in the plate joints below.
A brick goat stands on the roof of the chase trailer, all four hooves planted wide, the smooth unmarked trailer flank rocking visibly side to side with each small shift of weight.
A loose packed-up balloon balloons up off the green plate mosaic and rolls over in a slow half-turn, its curved slope bricks catching air and lifting one end high off the ground.
A runaway brick picnic hamper bounces down the grass slope, one wheel already off its axle pin, red apple studs and a round-brick orange spilling ahead of it in a rolling scatter.
A gust flattens a broad fan of tuft elements hard across the green plate mosaic and throws a wide low arc of tan studs up off the plates into the air.
A rainbow of stacked trans-plate arcs stands against the dark half of the sky, each colour layer a separate plate row, the outermost violet arc curving just past the crown of the nearest balloon.
White plate-flecks sheet upward in a low rooster-tail behind a basket dragging through snow plates, the drag groove it cuts stretching back in a clean straight furrow across the white field.
A spray of trans-blue plates throws up where a basket clips the pond edge, the plates fanning outward and catching light before falling back across the trans-blue plate surface below.
One balloon settles slowly into a broad oak, the moulded plant-element branches bending under the curved slope bricks and a cascade of small leaf plates shaking loose and spiralling down.
A brick beehive teeters on its post for one long moment before going over, yellow studs pouring out in a thick stream that fans across three rows of green plate mosaic.
A loose scatter of tan studs lifts off the plates in a gust and hangs at knee height for a moment before the wind carries them sideways across the field in a drifting veil.
A stack of smooth unmarked round-brick gas cylinders topples in a slow diagonal, the last cylinder bouncing twice on the plate mosaic and coming to rest against a moulded tuft clump.
A brick dog hits the end of the trailing rope at full stretch and spins sideways, all four legs leaving the plate mosaic at once before it scrambles back to its feet and bolts again.
A tarpaulin element peels off a trailer roof, turns once in the air above the smooth unmarked trailer flank, and plasters itself over a run of hedgerow bricks with a muffled crump.
